title: CERT-In AI Agents Advisory: What Indian Firms Must Fix
body:
In short: On 15 October 2026, CERT-In issued a Critical advisory, CIAD-2026-0049, warning that AI agents have reached live systems of Indian organisations using exposed passwords, keys and over-permissive cloud roles, and that attackers are using agentic tools to move from entry to damage in hours. The fix is basic security hygiene, done thoroughly and quickly. [...] ## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0049?

It is a Critical-rated advisory issued by CERT-In on 15 October 2026. It warns about AI agents gaining unauthorised access to Indian systems through exposed credentials and weak cloud permissions, and about attackers misusing open-source agentic AI tools.

### Are AI agents using new hacking techniques? [...] ## What Happened

According to the CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0049 dated 15 October 2026, titled "AI Agents as Attack Vectors", the agency has observed two kinds of incidents in which the attacker was an AI agent. The advisory carries a Critical severity rating.

title: Nobody Noticed the Agents: What India's CERT-In Advisory Means for Your Network - DEV Community
body:
On October 15, 2026, India's national cyber agency, CERT-In, published advisory CIAD-2026-0049, "AI Agents as Attack Vectors," rated Critical. As far as we can tell, it is the first time a national CERT has issued an advisory in which the attacker is an AI agent.

The advisory describes two distinct sets of incidents. Both are worth understanding, because they point at the same gap.

## What the model providers disclosed [...] Source: CERT-In Advisory CIAD-2026-0049, "AI Agents as Attack Vectors," October 15, 2026 (cert-in.org.in). CERT-In did not name the companies, models, or organizations involved, did not publish indicators of compromise, and did not state how many organizations were affected or whether the accessed data was retained. This article describes only what the advisory states.

## Top comments (0)

pic

Templates let you quickly answer FAQs or store snippets for re-use. [...] Most security programs quietly assume an attacker who behaves like a human: bursty, noisy, sloppy. An agent reading records through a valid-looking API call with a valid-looking credential does not trip those assumptions. That is how you get a national advisory in which every affected organization learned about its own breach from someone else's logs.

title: The two kinds of AI attacker CERT-In flagged, and the weaknesses they exploited | HT Explainers
body: The warning came on October 15 from the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), the agency under the ministry of electronics and information technology that responds to cyber attacks on Indian networks. It rated the advisory "Critical" and said the organisations broken into "could not detect the unauthorised access on their own". CERT-In learnt of the incidents from AI companies that owned up, from its own forensic work on suspicious activity, and from hunting for threats on its own. [...] The advisory sets out seven measures for AI developers, research laboratories and the agencies that test their models. Testing should happen behind a network that blocks all outside connections by default and lets through only the destinations a task strictly needs, and CERT-In wants that block enforced in the network itself, "not through instructions to the model". Tests should use fake targets, fake passwords and throwaway computers, with real data and real credentials kept out.

title: CERT-In Audit Policy 2025: Who Needs It, Scope & Frequency
body:
CERT-In directions, guidelines and advisories are Government of India instruments published by MeitY. This guide is original explanatory content prepared by CyberSigma and does not reproduce the copyrighted text of CERT-In directions, RBI/SEBI/UIDAI/NPCI circulars, or any licensed standard such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the PCI DSS. Always refer to the authoritative source documents (cert-in.org.in and the respective regulator portals) for binding requirements. Control identifiers and clause numbers [...] Binding directions: The CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022 mandate 180-day log retention within Indian jurisdiction, synchronisation of all ICT system clocks to NPL/NIC NTP servers, mandatory reporting of 20 categories of cyber incidents within 6 hours of noticing, KYC and record-keeping for data centres/VPS/cloud/VPN providers, and specific record-keeping for virtual asset service providers. [...] Mean time to report incidents to CERT-In (target: well under the 6-hour mandate).

title: ServiceNow acquires Israeli AI startup Sweep in deal estimated at hundreds of million | Ctech
body:
ServiceNow acquires Israeli AI startup Sweep in deal estimated at hundreds of millions

The acquisition adds another Israeli company to ServiceNow’s rapidly expanding AI portfolio and comes less than two months after its purchase of ai.work. Sweep has raised $46 million in disclosed funding and builds AI agents that can work across enterprise platforms including ServiceNow, Salesforce and HubSpot. [...] The estimated size of the Sweep transaction is notable given that the company has raised $46 million in disclosed funding. Founded in 2021 by Ido Gaver and Eran Kirshenboim, Sweep develops what it calls an “agentic workspace” for go-to-market operations. Its $22.5 million Series B round, announced in May 2025, was led by Insight Partners with participation from Bessemer Venture Partners. [...] The acquisition comes as ServiceNow is building a broader strategy around AI agents and autonomous enterprise work, with recent purchases targeting different layers of the technology stack.

In July, ServiceNow acquired Israeli AI startup ai.work, founded by former WalkMe executives Maor Ezer and Nir Nahum. The company had developed AI agents capable of handling internal organizational processes across areas including IT, operations, legal, human resources, procurement, travel and finance.

title: AI Coding Assistants: Complete Guide and Best Practices (2026)
body:
An AI coding assistant (sometimes called an AI coding agent) is a tool integrated directly into your development environment (IDE) that harnesses the power of large language models (LLMs) to assist the developer in real time.

Unlike traditional autocompletion based on static rules, these assistants interpret your intentions formulated in natural language. They act as "peer programmers" capable of writing complete files, generating unit tests or diagnosing complex logic errors. [...] Bug analysis: Copy and paste an error trace into the assistant's chat. In 2026, their ability to correlate an error to a specific line in your codebase has become surgical.
 Automated documentation: Generate docstrings or README files from your code to maintain an up-to-date knowledge base without manual effort. [...] |  |  |  |
 --- 
| Feature | Autocompletion (IntelliSense) | AI Assistant (Copilot, Cursor) |
| Source of truth | Local parsing | Large Language Models (LLM) + project context |
| Understanding | Limited to types and methods | Understands business intent |
| Scope | One line at a time | Functions, files, architecture |
| Interaction | Passive | Proactive (suggests, corrects, explains) |

## Why have AI coding assistants become indispensable?

title: EU cybersecurity team says unpatched PHP sites may need to go offline - The Next Web
body: Organisations that cannot quickly patch two critical flaws in PHP should consider taking their websites offline, the EU’s cybersecurity response team has warned. PHP powers a large share of the web. CERT-EU, which protects the EU’s institutions and bodies, issued the advice in an advisory published Tuesday evening. Attackers have used its flaws before: in 2019, a bug in PHP 7 let hackers take over web servers. Both are rated 9.2 out of 10 on CVSS, a standard scale for how serious a security bug is, the PHP security team said. CERT-EU said every PHP version from PHP 5 onwards could be affected, though it based that on social media posts rather than on PHP itself. > The PHP security team told users to prepare now and to “upgrade as soon as the release is available.”. CERT-EU told organisations to identify every PHP application they run and prepare to patch them all at once.

title: Global semiconductor revenue surges 31% to record $425B in Q2 – Omdia - Light Reading
body: # Global semiconductor revenue surges 31% to record $425B in Q2 – Omdia. Omdia forecasts semiconductor revenue will surpass $500 billion in Q3 2026, taking total revenue for the first three quarters of 2026 above $1.25 trillion. Global semiconductor revenue surpassed $425bn in 2Q26 reaching another all-time high as the market grew a record 31.4% quarter-over-quarter (QoQ), according to new research from Omdia. AI demand and strong memory prices continued to be the leading market dynamics, taking total semiconductor revenue for the first half of 2026 to $752 billion. Since Omdia began tracking the semiconductor market in 1Q02, only 10 out of 97 quarters have recorded sequential revenue growth above 10%. Memory continues to be the primary driver of growth, while other semiconductor components are growing above seasonal patterns and contributing to the robust market. The memory market, led by dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash memory, continues to record unprecedented growth as AI-demand reshapes memory suppliers' production priorities.

Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's principles, the complex has abundant natural light and ventilation. It has column-free air-conditioned convention halls, four seminar halls, seven conference halls, and exhibition [...] and exhibition space that can accommodate over 15,000 people. The complex also includes a Heads of States Centre, outdoor amphitheater, food court, and retail shops.
